## `mainframe.adapter.physical_channel.status.code`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.adapter.physical_channel.status.code` | Gauge | `1` | The physical channel status of the mainframe I/O adapter as a numeric code. [1] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `mainframe.adapter` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[1]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API Adapter object property `physical-channel-status` (DPM mode only, HMC >= 2.13.1) via GET /api/adapters/{adapter-id}. Encoded as: 0=operating, 1=no-power, 2=service, 3=stopped, 4=not-defined, 5=definition-error, 6=suspended, 7=check-stopped, 8=wrap-block, 9=permanent-error, 10=loss-of-signal, 11=loss-of-synchronization, 12=not-operational-link, 99=unknown.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.adapter.id`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-adapter-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The physical channel identifier (PCHID) of the I/O adapter. [1] | `014`; `15C`; `1D8` |

**[1] `mainframe.adapter.id`:** The PCHID is the hexadecimal location of the adapter in the Central Processing Complex (CPC) and is unique within one CPC. Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `adapter-id`.

| `not-active` | The adapter is not active. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `not-detected` | The adapter is not detected by the system. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `service` | The adapter is in service mode. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.adapter.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.adapter.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the mainframe I/O adapter was busy processing I/O or requests, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [3] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `mainframe.adapter` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[3]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API. In DPM mode, source is the `adapter-usage` metric group field `adapter-usage`. In classic mode, sources are `crypto-usage` field `adapter-usage` (HMC >= 2.12.0), `flash-memory-usage` field `adapter-usage` (HMC >= 2.12.0). SC27-2646-01 v2.17.0 declares no `roce-usage` metric group; RoCE adapter utilization is reported through the DPM `adapter-usage` group. Note that the classic-mode `crypto-usage` and `flash-memory-usage` groups have Applicable Managed Object Class `cpc`, not `adapter`: one entry is produced per adapter, and the adapter identity must be reconstructed from the in-group `channel-id` (and `crypto-id` for cryptos) rather than taken from the object the metric group is attached to. The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. Use `mainframe.adapter.type` to distinguish adapter categories. Analogous to NIC, HBA, or RDMA NIC utilization.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.adapter.id`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-adapter-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The physical channel identifier (PCHID) of the I/O adapter. [4] | `014`; `15C`; `1D8` |
| [`mainframe.adapter.type`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-adapter-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The type of the mainframe I/O adapter card. [5] | `crypto`; `flash`; `roce` |

**[4] `mainframe.adapter.id`:** The PCHID is the hexadecimal location of the adapter in the Central Processing Complex (CPC) and is unique within one CPC. Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `adapter-id`.

**[5] `mainframe.adapter.type`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API adapter object field `type`. Used to distinguish network, storage, cryptographic, and accelerator adapters when aggregating per-type utilization metrics.

---

`mainframe.adapter.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accelerator` | An accelerator adapter, providing hardware acceleration for specific workloads such as compression or AI inference. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `crypto` | A cryptographic (crypto) adapter, providing hardware-accelerated encryption and key management. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `flash` | A Flash Express adapter, providing solid-state storage for IBM Virtual Flash Memory (VFM). | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `network` | A network adapter providing connectivity to external networks. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `roce` | A RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE) adapter, providing low-latency RDMA networking over Ethernet. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `storage` | A storage adapter providing connectivity to external storage systems such as SAN or NVMe-oF. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.channel.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.channel.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the I/O channel path was busy processing I/O, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [4] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `mainframe.channel` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[4]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API channel-usage metric group field `channel-usage` (classic mode). The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. A channel path identifier (CHPID) is the unique identifier for a hardware I/O channel. Use the `mainframe.channel.name` attribute in CSS.CHPID format to identify the specific channel path. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the link utilization of a network interface or storage HBA port.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.channel.name`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-channel-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the I/O channel in the form CSS.Chpid. [6] | `0.00`; `0.2D`; `1.E3` |
| [`mainframe.channel.mode`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-channel-mode) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operating mode of the I/O channel — either dedicated to a single partition or shared across partitions. | `dedicated`; `shared` |

**[6] `mainframe.channel.name`:** The channel subsystem (CSS) index and channel path identifier (CHPID) are concatenated with a dot separator, e.g., "0.2D" for CSS 0, CHPID 2D. Reported by the HMC Web Services API channel-path object.

---

`mainframe.channel.mode` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dedicated` | The I/O channel is dedicated to a specific partition and cannot be shared with other partitions. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `shared` | The I/O channel can be shared among multiple partitions and is not dedicated to a specific partition. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.cpu.smt_mode.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.cpu.smt_mode.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time the processor was running in simultaneous multithreading (SMT) mode, as a ratio from 0 to 1. [5] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `mainframe.cpu` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[5]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC metric group `zcpc-processor-usage` field `smt-usage` (all modes). A value of -1 indicates that the mainframe model does not support simultaneous multithreading (SMT). When SMT is active, a single physical processor executes two hardware threads concurrently (SMT-2), improving instruction throughput.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |

| [`mainframe.cpu.name`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-cpu-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the mainframe processor, formed as the processor type abbreviation followed by the processor index number. [7] | `IFL01`; `CP02`; `zIIP03` |

**[7] `mainframe.cpu.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API processor object. In distributed systems terms, a mainframe processor is analogous to a physical CPU core.

## `mainframe.cpu.utilization`

The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. Provides individual physical-processor-level telemetry, unlike `mainframe.host.cpu.utilization` which reports a CPC-level aggregate. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to per-core CPU utilization from a system performance tool.
